body: SABIT ULLAH t: The petitioners have invoked the constitutional jurisdiction of this Court under Article 199 of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973. They call in question the judgment dated 12.01 .2026 of the learned Additional District Judge-I, Karak, whereby their Civil Revision No. 16/CR of 2024 was dismissed. That judgment upheld the order dated 08.05.2024 of the learned Senior Civil Judge-II, Karak, which restored the respondents' proceedings under Section 12(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 ("the Code"). The lis traces back to Civil Suit No. 42811 of 1979, "Gul Khameen versus Abdullah Khan", which was partly dccrccd on 08.12.1983 to the extent of 1501240 shares in the suit property. Decadcs later, the respondents assailed that decree on the allegation of fraud and (S,B) HON'BLE MR, JUSTICESABIT ULLAH KHAN misrepresentation. Their application under Section l2(2) of the Code was dismissed by the trial Court on 28.03.2019. The revisional Court, however, remanded the matter on 24.10.2019 for decision afresh after framing of issues and recording of evidence. This Court, in Writ Petition No. 218-B of 2020 decided on 16.09.2021, set aside the rcmand order and dismissed the application under Section l2(2) of the Codc as misconceived.

2. The respondents challenged that judgment before the Hon'ble Supreme Court of Pakistan inCivil PetitionNo,5726 of 2021, which was dismissed as not pressed on 27.10.2023. Treating the direction recorded in that order as a mandate to revive their application, the respondents sought restoration of the proceedings bcfore thc trial Cour1. 'l'hat praycr was granted on 08.05.2024 and affirmed in revision on 12.01.2026. The sole question for determination is this: could a subordinate Court restore proceedings that stood dismissed by a judgment of this Court, when no competent superior forum had set aside, modified or recalled that judgment? Answering it requires an examination of the true import olthe order of the apex Court.

3, Undcr Article 201 of the Constitution, a judgment of a lligh Courl binds every Court subordinate to it until it is set aside, modified or recalled by a competent forum in accordance with law. Under the doctrine of merger, the decision of a lower forum merges into that ofthe higher forum only where the latter adjudicates upon the merits. A petition for leave to appeal that is withdrawn or not pressed results in no adjudication and, (S.B) HON'BLE R JUST]CE SABIT UL J ( consequently, no merger. In that event, the judgment of the High Court holds the field in its own right and attains finality. l'he ordcr of thc Hon'ble Supreme Court dated 27.10.2023, in its relevant part, reads: " After arguing the case at some length, learned counsel for the petitioner does not press lhis petition but requests that lhe Trial Court may be directed to decide the matter expeditiously 2 In view of the above, this petition is dismissed as not pressed However, the Trial Court is directed to proceed with the matter expeditiously and after framing the issues, decide the same strictly in accordance with law preferably within a period of ninety days (90)
from the receipt of certified copy of this order."

A plain reading of the order shows that leave was neither granted nor refused on merits. The judgment of this Court was not disturbed, and thc application under Section l2(2) ofthe code was not revived. The direction that follows was made on the request of the respondents' own counsel, in the absence of the present petitioners and without any adjudication. It is procedural in nature. It regulates the pace at which a lawfully pending matteristobedecidcd;itcannotcreatealiswhcrenoncsubsisls'l'hc reference to framing of issues must be read in that context' Had the apex Court intended to resurrect the proceedings, it would have converted the petition into an appeal and set aside the judgment of this Court; it did neither. Moreover, by declining to press their petition after arguing it at length, the respondents acquiesced in the judgment dated 16'09'2021' They could not reopen before a subordinate Court what thcy had (S.B) HON'BLE MR, JUST\CESABIT ULLAH KHAN { consciously abandoned before the apex Court. If they believed the direction carried a wider meaning, their remedy lay in seeking clarification from the Hon'ble Supreme Court itself, not in inviting the Courts below to supply that meaning by inference.

4. Reliance on Article I 89 of the Constitution is equally misplaoed That Article makes a decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Courl binding only to the extent that it decides a question oflaw or is based upon or enunciates a principle of law. An order dismissing a petition as not pressed decidcs no such question. The Code, moreover, contains no provision for restoring proceedings that a superior Court has dismissed on merits. The inherent powers under Section 1 5 I of the Code exist to advance justice within the bounds of law, no1 to defeal a judgmcnt that has attaincd finalily. 'l'hc principle of finality underlying Section 1l of the Code applies with cqual force between successive stages of the same proceedings. The leamed Senior Civil Judge-II, Karak, therefore assumed a jurisdiction not vested in him when he treated a direction for expeditious disposal as an ordcr reviving concluded proceedings. The leamed revisional Court, in tum, failed to exercise the jurisdiction vested in it under Section 115 of the Code to correct that error. Both thus acted illegally and with malcrial irregularity. Concurrent orders passed without lawful authority attract no immunity from interference, and as no further remedy lies against the revisional judgment, the constitutional jurisdiction of this Court has rightly been invoked (s. ts) HON'BLE MII. J SABIT I]I,I,AH KHAN 5. For the foregoing reasons, this writ petition is allowed. 'l-he judgment dated 12.01.2026 of the leamed Additional District Judge-I, Karak, and the order dated 08.05.2024 of the leamed Senior Civil Judge- II, Karak, are set aside. Consequently, the respondents' application lbr restoration ofthe proceedings under Section 12(2) ofthe Code shall stand dismissed, the judgment of this Court dated 16.09.2021 in Writ Petition No. 21 8-B of 2020 holding the field.
